sampling_model.design: A fixed finite population is partitioned into \(m\) labeled clusters; the chosen law \(D\) randomizes jointly over cluster saturation labels and exact treated subsets.
sampling_model.units: Potential outcomes \(Y_{g i}(z,a)\) are fixed; there is no superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: Cluster \(g\) receives label \(A_g\), then exactly \(r_{s_g,A_g}\) of its \(s_g\) units are treated.
sampling_model.overlap: The general results allow every feasible count \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant menus. Interiority is imposed only for the stated forbidden-triple, strict-separation, and complement-symmetry regimes; saturation variation is imposed only for the last two. Optimal designs may assign zero probability to labels or assignment orbits.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the estimator is chosen jointly with the randomization and may be nonlinear in the revealed outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 derives standard errors and power criteria for individual saturation and slope effects under a clustered regression model.
Theorem 1 shows that independent fair assignment with a nonlinear estimator is minimax over bounded no-interference potential outcomes.
Theorem 2.3 Bernoulli-lifts the binary no-interference minimax experiment to bounded outcomes and decodes a nonlinear rule.
Proposition 2.2 expresses the arbitrary-neighborhood-interference minimax risk as a function of a pairwise conflict graph.
The paper optimizes bias and variance of the difference-in-means estimator across randomized saturation designs under a linear interference model.
Theorem 2.1 proves minimax complete randomization by group averaging under permutation invariance for a fixed invariant estimator.

body.tldr: Randomized saturation experiments reveal overlapping vectors of own-treatment-by-saturation responses, so their unrestricted design-and-estimation problem is neither a no-interference tensor product nor a pairwise conflict-graph game. For fixed saturation count and bounded cluster size, every feasible treated-count table, including boundary counts and a label-constant menu, reduces exactly to a rational endpoint orbit game over all correlated designs, bounded schedules, and measurable estimators. Conditional uniform subset randomization is without loss, independent-saturation minimaxity has a finite primal-dual characterization, and the certified two-cluster instance has a strict correlated-saturation advantage on an infinite rational contrast neighborhood. The orbit game is now algorithmic in the Turing model: global rational primal and dual oracles, explicit nested polytopes, and strictly eroded mixed comparators yield polynomial-time weak optimization, outward-rounded risk certificates, and a total division-free continuous-estimator decoder, without claiming rational exact optimizers.

project_justification.gap: Saturation-design papers optimize power or the bias and variance of specified regression or inverse-probability estimators, while recent unrestricted minimax papers either assume no interference or replace observation feasibility by a pairwise conflict graph. None preserves the exact-count observation hypergraph while jointly optimizing the first-stage law and an arbitrary measurable estimator across the full feasible menu, including zero, full, and label-constant treated counts.
project_justification.niche: Fixed saturation-label count and bounded cluster size leave exponentially many labeled schedules but only polynomially many size-tagged response, assignment, and observation histograms, whether treated counts are interior, on the boundary, or constant across labels. That symmetry permits an exact decision-theoretic quotient without assuming independence or linearity.
project_justification.fill: The paper establishes endpoint completeness and a stabilizer-weighted rational primal-dual orbit game for every feasible count table, with implementable correlated randomization and nonlinear estimation. It gives a finite independent-design frontier, a strict rational separation certificate, and a bit-certified compiler. The compiler uses exact global perspective and bounded-decision oracles, explicit rational inner and outer polytopes, and face-by-face erosion comparators to return checkable rational \(\varepsilon\)-saddles and a total zero-face-safe decoder in time polynomial in the displayed orbit-program size, input bit length, and \(\log\max\{2,1/\varepsilon\}\).

body.related_work: BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018 provides the motivating fixed-count randomized-saturation design and its direct and spillover analysis, but not an unrestricted finite-population minimax estimator or a bit-certified joint design algorithm. Kallus2021 establishes mixed-strategy design optimality at a general decision-theoretic level, while the present result constructs and weakly optimizes the exact rational observation-hypergraph quotient. KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies a different pairwise conflict-graph design problem and gives a polynomial approximation there; the present kernel retains higher-order exact-count observation compatibility. Hull2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026 supply endpoint reductions in no-interference experiments, whereas the present compiler covers bounded anonymous saturation interference, arbitrary correlated first-stage laws, boundary treated counts, and label-constant menus. HudgensHalloran2008, BasseFeller2018, and JiangImaiMalani2023 provide the design-based two-stage causal framework but do not jointly optimize arbitrary estimators and correlated saturation laws.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The compiler guarantee is polynomial in the displayed orbit-program size for fixed \(K\) and \(b\); it does not make the constant-size response alphabet small in practice and is not a strongly polynomial algorithm. Exact rational arithmetic may produce large certificates even though their bit length is polynomial. The numerical size-three witness remains supported by its separate exhaustive rational verifier, while the compiler theorem supplies the general symbolic kernel construction, global oracle geometry, erosion-correct weak optimization, tolerance accounting, and decoder proof rather than a new numerical rerun.
body.honest_scope: Endpoint completeness, the exact orbit game, and the bit-certified compiler cover every rational feasible table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant treated-count menus. The compiler returns rational weakly optimal primal and dual certificates and a total continuous estimator; it does not claim that exact optimizers are rational, an elementary closed-form classification of the independent-saturation frontier, or a separation as the number of clusters tends to infinity. The strict advantage remains the certified two-cluster instance and its infinite rational contrast neighborhood, and its proof uses the full exact-count observation hypergraph.
body.interpretation: For a fixed menu of saturation labels and bounded cluster sizes, an experimental team can compile the exact finite observation experiment rather than approximate it by pairwise conflicts. Rational weights specify how to randomize saturation histograms and treated subsets, the endpoint table specifies a possibly nonlinear analysis rule, and two directly checkable rational inequalities bracket the worst-case causal mean-squared error within any requested rational tolerance. The continuous-outcome rule is a finite Bernoulli-histogram polynomial, so structurally impossible or prior-null observations never trigger an undefined posterior ratio.
